lines.en: In the Florentine codices, in which astrological matters are preserved, we have followed this order in reviewing them:
viewed, we have followed this order:

lines.text: I. Codices qui singulorum scriptorum opera continent inspeximus;
lines.en: I. We have inspected the codices which contain the works of individual writers;

lines.text: II. Codices qui collectanea astrologica appellari possunt descrip-
lines.en: II. We have described the codices which can be called astrological collections;

lines.text: III. Codices qui nonnullis foliis tantum excerpta ad astrologiam
lines.en: III. We have noted the codices which offer only excerpts pertaining to astrology on a few leaves.

lines.text: Fieri quidem potest ut praeter ea quae hic recensenda curavi,
lines.en: It is indeed possible that besides those which I have taken care to review here, others lie hidden in the Laurentian Library; however, I would contend that very few lie hidden; for with the utmost diligence and patience I have surveyed all that pertained to the undertaking. We have added some unpublished fragments, others by learned men whose names are individually signed.

lines.en: I was writing at Senigallia on the 4th day before the Nones of November in the year 1897.

summary.headline: Review of the Florentine Codices
summary.text: A. Olivieri explains his review of Florentine astrological codices: individual authors’ works, astrological collections, and codices containing only excerpts. He notes unpublished fragments and assistance from Fr. Cumont, and dates the preface to Senigallia, 4 November 1897.
